records.name: Ed25519 base-field multiplication
records.summary: Ordinary-domain centered-radix-32 multiplication modulo 2^255-19 with an exact pseudo-Mersenne quotient/carry certificate, plus zero-hint eight-word decoders to certified digits or centered limbs.
records.security: Operands passed to the compact gate must already be certified canonical 51-digit values from the same verified path; the raw wrapper performs that certification for hostile witness operands. Thirteen signed tables bind all 663 selected products to the left operand. One scalar quotient and 50 carries prove the exact integer relation after the 32^51 = p+19 fold. Script derives every result digit, range-checks it, rejects the 19 noncanonical radix vectors, and returns the unique ordinary-domain residue. This field gate alone provides no EdDSA verification claim.
records.stack_contract: A value is 51 biased centered-radix-32 digits with digit zero nearest the top; the host API denotes ordinary residues in [0,p). Multiplication consumes lhs[50..0] | rhs[50..0] | quotient | carries[49..0], with carry zero nearest the top, and returns certified r[50..0]. Packed decoders consume eight coexisting compressed-u32 data items word7..word0 and return either sixteen centered limbs limb15..limb0 or fifty-one biased digits digit50..digit0. Both decoder variants require zero auxiliary hints per invocation and across the G32 schedule's 46 grouped and 47 digit invocations. The preserved-item argument counts unrelated combined main/altstack state; decoder-local peaks include their sixteen temporary script-authored powers.

records.name: Native secp256k1 base-field arithmetic
records.summary: Balanced-radix secp256k1 multiplication and squaring with ordinary-domain and factor-16 Montgomery-domain normalized-Karatsuba profiles and exact witness-carried integer reduction.
records.security: Operands passed to compact gates must be verified-path outputs of the native field certificate or an earlier gate. The ordinary profile uses eleven quotient coefficients and 56 carries; factor-16 uses one residual and 28 carries. Script derives and certifies the remainder while checking one exact integer relation, so no CRT-wraparound assumption is used. Circuit authors must preserve the factor-16 E(x)=x/16 semantic domain.
records.stack_contract: A field value is 29 balanced radix-512 digits with digit zero nearest the top. Ordinary multiplication consumes certified lhs[28..0] | rhs[28..0] | q[10..0] | carries[55..0]; factor-16 consumes encoded lhs[28..0] | rhs[28..0] | t | carries[27..0]. Each returns certified r[28..0] in its own domain. Preserved-item arguments count unrelated main and altstack state.

records.name: Prime residue-number arithmetic
records.summary: Prime RNS profiles for exact unsigned 256-by-256-bit products, coordinate-major table-amortized batches, and fixed-modulus witness-hinted reduction, including compact conditional, standalone globally bound, and reusable-certificate composable verifiers.
records.security: Each combined modulus is composite, so exact-integer semantics require a proved expression bound. The coordinate-only hinted profiles, including the 42-prime carry verifier, are conditional on external global bindings for every supplied vector. The standalone 47-prime secp256k1-target profile range-checks four shared 16-limb values and closes all bindings locally. The 46-prime composable profile instead inherits certified lhs/rhs vectors from its own field-value binder or a prior multiplication, binds hostile q and r locally, and returns a certified r vector; passing raw witness residue vectors violates its soundness precondition. In both globally safe profiles, the product basis exceeds 2^512 and all exact ScriptNum prefixes are checked.
records.stack_contract: The no-carry profile uses 75 canonical residues and contiguous vectors. Its batch API consumes coordinate-major operand pairs and leaves coordinate-major products on the altstack. The conditional carry profile consumes 42 coordinate-interleaved groups lhs_i | rhs_i | q_i | r_i | [complement_i] | carry_i and returns 42 remainder residues. The standalone profile consumes 64 centered limbs followed by 47 five-carry groups and returns 16 centered remainder limbs beneath 47 canonical remainder residues. The composable gate consumes certified lhs[46] | rhs[46] | q_limbs[16] | r_limbs[16] | 46 reverse-coordinate three-carry groups and returns only certified r[46]; its preserved-item argument counts unrelated main and alt stack state.

records.name: BLAKE3 Ed25519-style challenge transcripts
records.summary: Checked-u4 BLAKE3 transcripts for a custom Ed25519-style verifier, including a strict-tested fixed-key, fixed-message one-compression form.
records.security: These configurations compute ordinary unkeyed BLAKE3 transcripts and return arithmetic u4 digits, but they define a custom signature challenge rather than RFC 8032 Ed25519. Runtime R and any runtime M digits must be bound by the surrounding protocol; the fixed-message form verifies its hostile M carrier against the compiled constant before consuming it. Fixed A must be the exact canonical public-key encoding used by the curve layer, and point/subgroup/scalar obligations remain external.
records.stack_contract: The exact-96 form consumes 192 checked u4 data items and the generic key-specialized form consumes 128. At the historical H16 fixed-message boundary, 337 preserved items plus R32 and M32 give 465 pair-entry items; the binder consumes M32, leaving 401 hash-frontier items. The G32 canonical-u5 helper receives 391 preserved items including all 51 R digits. Every form uses exactly zero auxiliary hint items. The fixed-message pair and canonical-u5 helper have strict combined peaks of 864 and 918; general-form peak statements remain analytic unless explicitly marked strict.

records.name: BLAKE3 Ed25519-style Montgomery slope verifier candidate
records.summary: Key-specialized custom Ed25519-subgroup signature candidate using an independently bias-127-recoded 128-bit BLAKE3 challenge and torsion-coset Montgomery u encoding, with historical G29 hinted/q-free leaves and a 47-transition G32 hybrid-u5 zero-hint successor.
records.security: This is a custom signature scheme, not RFC 8032. Every linked benchmark fixes M32, but that constant is not a transaction digest and provides no transaction authorization or replay protection. Its BLAKE3 public-key bytes equal the standard encoding of the point used by the compiled tables. The disclosed benchmark secret a=987654321 makes the exact fixture forgeable. The production-oriented host generator accepts and validates an external prime-subgroup public key without its secret, but no production transaction-binding or deployment workflow exists. Nonce derivation remains unspecified and nonce reuse with Ed25519 or another scheme under the same scalar would disclose the key. Rtilde is a canonical torsion-shifted Montgomery-u encoding. The hinted configuration must consume every recovered quotient and metadata bit; both q-free configurations derive the unique bounded quotients. The G29 q-free path relies on the final transition to certify packed-R words copied earlier by BLAKE3, while G32 checks the canonical u5 field during the hash copy and consumes the preserved original in its fused terminal relation. Every complete construction still needs independent cryptographic review and Bitcoin Core validation.
records.stack_contract: Hinted G29 baseline: all 704 packed trace-data items and all 88 logical quotient-hint items coexist at entry, 792 items total with no separate scalar/transcript items; its strict peak-equivalent schedule reaches 999. G29 q-free: 704 trace items plus eight scalar words, 712 data items total and exactly zero hints, all coexisting at entry, with an analytical 912-item maximum. Current G32 hybrid-u5: 795 trace items plus eight scalar words, exactly 803 coexisting entry-data items and zero auxiliary hints per each of 47 transitions and in total; its analytical combined main-plus-alt maximum is 999 including script-authored power pools, leaving one item of headroom. No multi-megabyte leaf was executed as a whole.

records.name: Ed25519 fixed-base scalar multiplication
records.summary: Canonical-scalar fixed-base [s]B using a 29-group centered-window table and 28 exact signed/identity-safe affine relation transitions.
records.security: The eight scalar words are checked against the exact canonical interval 0<=s<l. One scalar callback derives each signed digit, then its magnitude selects the constants and identity/nonzero control from an embedded position table, keeping sign and table selection bound to the same digit. Each hostile packed tau/next-point trace is canonicalized, and three exact integer H=q*p recurrences bind the transition; q is unique, so the integrated byte-minimizing path needs no separate signed-23-bit range decoder. The returned point is certified for this fixed-base schedule only; this fragment performs no point decoding, SHA-512 challenge, variable-base multiplication, final EdDSA equation, or terminal predicate.
records.stack_contract: At fragment entry, 672 trace circuit-data items, 84 direct quotient-hint items, and eight scalar words coexist: exactly 764 items. Each of 28 transitions consumes 24 trace items and three logical q hints; honest q occupies a signed 23-bit slot and at most three ScriptNum payload bytes. The fragment consumes all inputs and returns certified expanded x[50..0] | y[50..0] in 102 items.

records.name: BN254 field tower
records.summary: Fq, Fr, Fq2, Fq6, and Fq12 arithmetic over nine 29-bit limbs with witness hints.
records.security: Canonical field range and every hinted equation must be checked; field arithmetic alone has no protocol security claim.
records.stack_contract: Base fields use nine limbs; extension elements concatenate tower coefficients in source-defined order, and hinted calls place their returned ordered hints below the operands.
